title: WIST Delta Envelope (WIST-1)
description: Size-cap profiles follow WIST-1 section 3.6, Size-cap parameter time; this schema cannot select a validation-stage parameter map.

wist_version.description: Release-version spelling only. WIST-1 sections 3.1 and 7 separately require supported-major validation; minor and patch differences alone do not reject.

publisher.description: Signed Publisher identity under WIST-1 section 3.8; must equal its own Canonical Host. The pattern alone does not validate A-labels.

observed_at.description: WIST-1 section 3.4: Gregorian calendar validation, exact fractions and offsets, seconds 00–59 without leap-event data; year zero is valid. The pattern alone does not establish calendar validity.

payload.description: Salted commitment to the Delta's content (WIST-1 §3.6). The content itself travels as a Payload alongside the Epoch (WIST-3 §6.1) and never enters the Log.

bytes.description: Octets of JCS(content) = extract_cap_bytes + summary_cap_bytes + links_cap_bytes + the 32 octets of {"extract":,"links":,"summary":} structure that surround them (WIST-1 §3.6). It is a derived bound, not an independent constant.

lang.description: Lexical language-tag profile under WIST-1 section 3.7; no registry lookup, subtag ordering or uniqueness checks.

allOf.comment: WIST-1 §3.3: `new` and `update` are the content-bearing change types. One that commits to nothing claims content without saying what it is, and no Payload could ever be checked against it (WIST-1 §3.6) — WIST1-E09.
WIST-1 §3.3: `attest` and `delete` carry no content of their own; the chain they extend names the Payload that stands (WIST-3 §7).

WIST-1 §3.3: `update`, `delete` and `attest` each say something about a URL's earlier state, so each MUST name the Delta it follows. Only `new` may omit `prev`, and only when it is the very first Delta for that URL — a condition no schema can see, which is why `new` is absent from this branch and WIST1-E07 is where it is enforced.
